parsed_record.title: The list multiplicative 1-2-3 bound
parsed_record.statement: Let $G$ be a nice graph, and let $\operatorname{ch}_\Pi^*(G)$ denote the list parameter for the multiplicative labelling problem defined in the paper. **The list multiplicative 1-2-3 bound.** If $G$ is a nice graph, then $\operatorname{ch}_\Pi^*(G) \leq 3$. This is presented as a legitimate guess motivated by the List 1-2-3 Conjecture, rather than as an established conjecture; the supplied text gives no evidence that the bound is true or false.
parsed_record.source_name: Julien Bensmail, Hervé Hocquard, Dimitri Lajou and Éric Sopena, “On a List Variant of the Multiplicative 1-2-3 Conjecture”, arXiv:2102.08052 (2021).
parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.08052

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

parsed_record.title: The Conforti--Cornuéjols packing problem
parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a clutter. Its packing property means that every minor $\mathcal C'$ satisfies the König property, namely $\alpha_0(\mathcal C')=\beta_1(\mathcal C')$. The max-flow min-cut property is the standard corresponding flow-cut property for a clutter.

**Conforti--Cornuéjols packing problem.** A clutter $\mathcal C$ has the packing property if and only if it has the max-flow min-cut property.

The text states that the converse of the known implication from max-flow min-cut to packing is an unsolved conjecture.
parsed_record.source_name: Maria Vaz Pinto and Rafael H. Villarreal, “Graph rings and ideals: Wolmer Vasconcelos' contributions”, arXiv:2305.06270 (2025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.06270

parsed_record.title: Slicing Axes-Parallel Rectangles
parsed_record.statement: Let us say that two rectangles in the place are independent if both their $x$- and $y$-axis projections are disjoint. A set of rectangles is then independent if the rectangles are pairwise independent. Suppose that a collection of axes-parallel rectangles contains no independent set of size $m$ or greater. What is the minimal number, $f(m)$, of horizontal and vertical lines needed to slice every rectangle in the collection?
